text.p: - Despite international concern about President Yeltsin's health and rumours about financial problems at Russia's gas giant Gazprom, demand for its shares on world markets was much higher than expected.

- The newly appointed president of the National Sports Foundation, former Olympic Champion Vladimir Vasin, intends to turn it into an organisation open for public scrutiny. He would start with a thorough audit of its financial activities.
- The International Monetary Fund's tough position on allocating the next tranche of its loan to Russia is a sign of deep economic crisis in the country.

- President Yeltsin's appeal for reconciliation across the nation should first of all be addressed to the ruling authorities themselves, especially in the light of a growing power of the presidential administration.

- The presidents of Russia and Ukraine have declared that their countries are close to agreement over the division of the Black Sea fleet, although the parliaments of both countries made tough statements on this controversial issue on the eve of the summit.
- Elderly Russians cannot recieve their pensions because the country's biggest companies do not pay money to the Pension Fund wich is now short of 40 billion roubles.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's visit to the Federal Security Service on Wednesday and his speech there show the authorities are anticipating serious political problems.
- According to former Russian sports minister Shamil Tarpishchev, President Yeltsin's former security chief Alexander Korzhakov has been offered to the post as head of the sailing federation.
